actor_instance: Rayan executed Magnolia qualification and namespace cleanup; GPT-5.6 Sol diagnosed failures and encoded fixes
goal: Turn a successful one-off P100 qualification into a repeatable owner-scoped Magnolia runtime without rediscovering host/runtime incompatibilities or exposing project-facing names in shared scheduler/file views.
procedure: Diagnose host Python/glibc incompatibility; validate a Debian 12 Python 3.11 udocker runtime; reject per-Python-call container shims after recursion and MKL failures; retain the whole-stage single-container boundary that passed; rename Magnolia-visible runtime/container/log/job namespaces to rayan; keep internal ALICE interfaces stable; lock the owner compute tree to mode 700; encode the validated container boundary into tracked sbatch wrappers.
constraints: all Magnolia runtime artifacts remain under the owner's home compute tree
decision_criteria: no duplicate A.L.I.C.E-main clone under owner home
future sbatch wrappers use one udocker session
authority: Engineering/runtime and workspace-governance lesson only; no identity authority and no N1 authorization.
validation: 575524 failed from recursive python shim; 575525 failed during corpus-smoke with oneMKL/libtorch_cpu.so after per-call containerization; 575527 passed by running the entire stage inside one udocker session. Owner later verified rayan-compute, rayan-eipm-main, rayan-n0, udocker-store and udocker-tmp as drwx------ and found no old A.L.I.C.E-main clone under HOME.
failure_or_lesson: On legacy HPC hosts, containerization must be placed at the stage/process boundary, not blindly around each interpreter call. Namespacing and filesystem permissions are separate controls: use owner-identifying external names for collision avoidance and mode 700 for actual isolation while leaving internal software identifiers stable.
notes: Portable builder lesson: once a runtime boundary is empirically validated, encode that boundary directly in tracked launchers and record failed alternatives so future agents do not spend scarce accelerator time repeating them.
